In Planned Parenthood v. Casey, the Court affirmed [image: In Planned Parenthood v. Casey, the Court affirmed, “The ability of women to participate equally in the economic and social life of the Nation has been facilitated by their ability to control their reproductive lives.” A lot has happened since that historic moment. Contraception has become an essential part of how people plan their families, pursue their education and careers, care for the children they have, and decide if and when they’re ready to have more. And yet, access to contraception is still too often shaped by where you live, what you can afford, your health insurance, and the decisions of politicians and courts. On World Contraception Day (yesterday), we should remember what’s at stake: the freedom to decide if, when, and how to build a family is fundamental to being able to build the life you want. That freedom belongs to all of us. #PlatformOfCare #Contraception #ReproductiveRights #NorthCarolina #NCSenate]

Some bad bills aren’t bad in theory, they’re just [image: Some bad bills aren’t bad in theory, they’re just bad in implementation. When it comes to failing at implementation, House Bill 328 really takes the cake. This bill doesn’t keep anyone safer, but it does criminalize people for possessing hemp-derived consumables. The good news? Currently, there doesn’t seem to be an appetite to move this bill as written. If that changes, I’ll keep you posted. **Clarification: Hemp is the legal term for any product produced with 0.3% or less THC. In other words, we’re not talking about weed. #SophiaforNC #PlatformOfCare #DurhamNC #NCSenate #Hemp]
